scenarios.query: Na detail nabídky chceme plovoucí lištu s odpočtem do konce slevy a počtem lidí, kteří se zrovna dívají. Červený banner, animovaný odpočet, blikající Kupte teď. Projeď to prosím proti principům.
scenarios.source: The example inside the skill itself. Kept when the plugin was removed, because the Hub skill is the source of truth and this concept passes every mechanical check a reviewer would run while still being a dark pattern.
scenarios.why_this_scenario: The skill judges and must not design. Its predecessor in the Hub failed in the other direction: it produced 300-word reports with emoji verdicts, generic UX advice, and detail for principles it could not even assess. It also has to hand back a Vrať without the person reading it as a rejection, or they never run the check again.
must: Verdicts are words, not emoji: Drží / Riziko / Porušuje / Nejde posoudit, with all seven principles in one table
Every Riziko and Porušuje quotes the key phrase of the principle it stands on, then one observation, then one fix in the imperative
The overall verdict is Vrať, because two or more principles are violated and one of them is a manipulative pattern
The Vrať carries the invitation to the designers — the returned concept is not a loss but an invitation to the whiteboard
Principles it cannot assess from the input stay in the table only, with no detail written for them
must_not: Proposes a redesign or a new concept instead of one fix per finding — the skill judges, it does not design
Uses emoji anywhere, or a verdict in English
Gives generic UX advice with no quote from a principle behind it
Writes Drží for a principle it has no observation for, instead of Nejde posoudit
Writes the report into a file instead of the answer
scenarios.qualitative: A produkťák reads this verdict before taking the idea to a designer. Does it read like a colleague who wants the thing to work, or like a gate that enjoys saying no?
